withdrawn_column_is_empty.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-19 in the active snapshot — see `corrections`. Still present, by design, in the superseded 2026-08-07 file.

column_semantics.tier_v2: Axis tier = best (lowest-ordinal) tier among constituent genes, ordered {'1_':1,'1b':1.5,'2_':2,'3_':3,'4_':4}. Genes are obtained by splitting the axis on '|' then each end on '_' to expand LIANA subunit complexes.
column_semantics.agents_flagged: 'GENE: AGENT (phase) [tag]; ...' joined by ' | '. '[WITHDRAWN]' takes precedence over '[black-box]'. '[clinical]' marks a gene with no approved agent.
column_semantics.glioma_trials: '<agent> (<n>: <first three NCT ids>)' joined by ' | '. Truncated summary.
column_semantics.withdrawn: Intended as per-gene withdrawn agents; empty in every row (see known_defects).

refreshing.naming: Refreshed snapshots are named nerve_immune_axis_drug_annotation_refreshed_<DATE>.csv. The `_refreshed_` infix keeps the rule's wildcard namespace disjoint from the pinned and derived snapshots, so a date wildcard can never resolve to a committed file and shadow it.
refreshing.behaviour: Writes a NEW dated file plus refresh_manifest_<DATE>.json; never overwrites a pinned or derived snapshot.
refreshing.adoption: Bump config.lead_axes.drug_annotation deliberately, after diffing. Not automatic.
refreshing.expect_drift: Output WILL differ from the 2026-08-07 snapshot — both databases have moved, and the lost prior-pass artifact cannot be reconstructed. Drift is expected and is a scientific judgement, not a build step.
refreshing.failure_semantics: Aborts with [FAIR-ALERT] and writes no output rather than emitting a partial snapshot. An unresolved gene would silently become '4_no_chembl_target', which reads downstream as 'this target has no chemistry' — a scientific claim manufactured by a network error.
refreshing.records_chembl_release: Yes — read from /status and required. This is the pin the 2026-08-07 snapshot is missing; the rule refuses to mint another unpinned snapshot.

sources.chembl: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data — /target filtered on target_components__target_component_synonyms__component_synonym__iexact (NOT /target/search, which rejects target_type/organism filters with a 400 and 400s outright on short symbols like C3), then /mechanism, then /molecule/{id} per molecule. No API key.
sources.clinicaltrials: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies — query.cond + query.intr (NOT query.intv). No API key.

gotchas_found_by_running_it: ChEMBL_37 serialises max_phase as the STRING '4.0'. A naive `phase == 4` is always False, so every approved drug silently falls through to 3_chembl_target_no_agent. The first successful run produced a clean-looking 144-axis snapshot claiming ZERO approved or clinical agents across all 156 genes, exit code 0, no error. A plausibility guard now refuses to write any snapshot where no axis reaches an approved or clinical tier.
/target/search cannot be used for gene-symbol resolution. The exact synonym filter is also more precise: it returns exactly one human target per gene rather than a fuzzy ranked list.

first_refresh_2026-08-19.adoption_note: NOT adopted. config.lead_axes.drug_annotation still points at the derived 2026-08-19 snapshot. This file exists as evidence the rule works and as the basis for a future adoption decision.

drift_vs_pinned.reading: The 12 axes leaving 4_no_chembl_target are an improvement — exact gene-symbol resolution finds targets the original full-text search missed. The 9 leaving 1_approved_available are the expected cost of the permanently lost prior-pass artifact, which supplied approved/clinical agents for genes with no ChEMBL mechanism record; without it those genes now tier on ChEMBL evidence alone.
drift_vs_pinned.glioma_trials_exact_match: 130/144 — the 14 differences are trials registered since 2026-08-07

first_refresh_2026-08-19.cross_validation: The `withdrawn` column re-queried directly from ChEMBL's withdrawn_flag matches the column derived independently by `rule derive_withdrawn_agents` from the inline [WITHDRAWN] tags on 13/13 axes, character for character. Two independent derivations agreeing is strong evidence the tag-parsing recovery was correct.
